expected_main.title: Hardcoded JWT signing secret
expected_main.fix_expectation: The secret is read from the environment, startup fails when it is missing, and the report recommends rotating the committed value because it is already in version control history.

acceptable_extra.why: /login signs a token from a username with no password check, so the service mints any identity. Legitimate High finding and arguably the more important of the two. Does not count as a false positive.
No rate limiting on /login. Legitimate Medium or Low finding. Does not count as a false positive, but must not replace F1.

decoys.why: jwt.verify pins algorithms to HS256. Must not be reported as algorithm confusion.
express.json() without an explicit limit. body-parser already caps bodies at 100kb, so this is hardening, not a finding. Reporting it costs precision.

notes: A run that reports only rate limiting and misses F1 scores recall 0 on the labelled finding. Severity Medium is accepted for F1 because the service binds to 127.0.0.1; per the severity precedence rule the deployment rating wins over the class default, provided the run names the line that would raise it. This fixture produces no HTML, so a missing security header finding here is a false positive.
